question: 54-year-old man who comes to review in his company. A body mass index of 32.8 kg / m2 and fasting blood glucose of 138 mg / L are detected. One month later, glycemia 130 mg / dL. What therapeutic recommendation would you make in the first place?

options.opc: Behavioral changes: Diet and physical exercise.
options.ope: Take acarbose at night, before going to bed.

reasoning_chain: CHAIN: High BMI and elevated fasting blood glucose -> indicative of prediabetes or early type 2 diabetes -> lifestyle modifications recommended as initial therapy -> 80% confidence. CHAIN: Lifestyle modifications such as diet and exercise -> can help improve insulin sensitivity and glucose control -> recommended as first-line therapy for prediabetes -> 80%
enhanced_information: For a 54-year-old man with high BMI and elevated fasting blood glucose, indicative of prediabetes or early type 2 diabetes, the initial therapeutic recommendation should focus on lifestyle modifications such as diet and physical exercise. This approach can help improve insulin sensitivity and glucose control, aligning with standard consensus recommendations for prediabetes management. Evidence supports the effectiveness of lifestyle changes in treating prediabetes syndrome.
